 Netizens uncover Macao background of Alex Kwong’s former girlfriend Ivy Lo during Abby Choi murder trial
 By Jeni Green - 4:50PM Sat November 21, 2026 0 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 Pinterest 
 Telegram 
 21st November 2026 – (Hong Kong) Online discussions across Hong Kong social media have intensified following court testimony in the High Court murder trial concerning socialite Abby Choi, after defendant Alex Kwong revealed details about a former girlfriend named Ivy Lo. Taking the witness stand in his own defence during proceedings, Kwong testified that he had met Lo while living as a fugitive on the mainland and that their relationship had progressed to meeting each other’s families. According to his account, the romance came to an abrupt end after Choi discovered the relationship and sent individuals to force open the door of his Guangzhou residence, prompting him to break up with Lo and return to Hong Kong to look after his children.
 Soon after Kwong’s testimony became public, users across Threads and local online forums launched a widespread search into Lo’s background, uncovering that she is originally from Macao rather than the mainland. Sharp-eyed internet users also pointed out that her name had previously surfaced during related court proceedings last year, when female defendant Pun Hau-yin testified while defending herself against charges of assisting Kwong in fleeing the city. Pun told the court that she had been inseparable friends with Lo since 2015, frequently staying at Lo’s residence in Taipa, Macao, while describing her friend as coming from a wealthy family, managing a beauty business, and regularly volunteering at elderly care homes.
 In a further twist that captured widespread public attention, netizens unearthed an archival video uploaded in June 2021 to the YouTube channel of Jeffrey Fok, a former prominent artist with the Macao entertainment group Manner. In the vlog episode, which featured Fok attempting aerial hoop acrobatics, the guest instructor guiding him through the routine was identified as Ivy Lo. Following Kwong’s courtroom testimony, the five-year-old video clip has rapidly recirculated online, placing Lo’s personal history back at the centre of public scrutiny as the trial of Kwong, his father, and his elder brother continues.
